ImageDescription.value:
This waterfall is famous among all tourist in Iceland. Pretty much everyone stops here to take some photos. Situated in southern Iceland, it can already be seen from the Ring Road. The river Seljalandsá, having its origin underneath the glacier Eyjafjallajökull, drops here about 60 meters from a tall cliff that was once Icelands southern coastline.

A pathway leads all the way around the waterfall, offering great opportunities for photos. Be sure, however, that your equipment is weather-proof.

ImageDescription.value:
La Goðafoss est localisée dans la région de Mývatn, sur le fleuve Skjálfandafljót dans la région Nord-Est de l’Islande. La cascade fait 12 mètres de hauteur[1] sur 30 mètres de largeur. La vue la plus complète pour les touristes est celle sur la plateforme. En l'an 1000, lorsque que Þorgeir Ljósvetningagoði Þorkelsson (Thorgeir Ljosvetningagodi Thorkelsson) a fait du christianisme la religion officielle de l'Islande, a jetté ses idoles/statues de dieux de l’ancienne religion dans cette chute. Depuis, la cascade de Goðafoss est surnommée la cascade des dieux.

Fossholl, Région du Nord-Est, Islande

ImageDescription.value:
This waterfall is famous among all tourist in Iceland. Pretty much everyone stops here to take some photos. Situated in southern Iceland, it can already be seen from the Ring Road. The river Seljalandsá, having its origin underneath the glacier Eyjafjallajökull, drops here about 60 meters from a tall cliff that was once Icelands southern coastline.

A pathway leads all the way around the waterfall, offering great opportunities for photos. Be sure, however, that your equipment is weather-proof.
